title: WODin workout plan
description: A prescribed workout, written by an agent and rendered as a loggable page. Everything here is the plan; what the athlete actually did comes back in result.schema.json.

workoutId.description: Stable id for this workout. A date (2026-09-13) is the usual choice; it is what the result references and what local autosave is keyed on.

athleteTitle.description: The athlete's standing banner, shown as the page's primary heading — e.g. "Odin's WOD". Constant across workouts. If omitted, `title` is promoted to the primary heading.

title.description: What this particular workout is — e.g. "Routine 2 — Back + Biceps".

program.description: Where this sits in a larger arc — e.g. "Foundation Return · Week 2 of 8".

targetRpe.description: Prescribed effort. Shown as a ghost hint ("Rx 7") on the blank session-RPE field; never prefilled as an answer.

rpe.description: Whether to ask for the session RPE. Absent: ask — unless every section has a `benchmark`, in which case 11 is assumed, because a day of girls and heroes is max effort with nothing left to rate. See $defs/rpeSetting.

coach.description: Who wrote this workout — a person, a gym, or the agent itself. Rendered as an attribution beneath the coach note, so a workout that gets shared onward still says where it came from.

coachNote.description: Free text from the agent to the athlete, rendered as a blockquote under the heading. The right home for session context — sleep, rest days, location, niggles, how to scale.

units.description: Document-wide defaults. Every rendered field shows its unit, so these are never implicit.

sink.description: Where a submitted result should go. Omit for the default, which offers share / copy / download. Everything here travels inside the link, so treat it as public.

url.description: Required when type is "post". The page POSTs the result JSON here.

mode.description: cors: normal JSON POST — the endpoint must answer the OPTIONS preflight and allow the headers used, and delivery is confirmed. blind: a no-cors POST that reaches an endpoint knowing nothing about CORS with no server changes, at the cost of an opaque response — the page cannot confirm delivery and does not claim to. headers are dropped in blind mode, which no-cors forbids.

headers.description: Extra request headers, for routing an athlete or program to the right handler. WARNING: the plan travels inside a shareable URL and is stored on the athlete's device, so anything here is public — a credential placed here is published, not protected. Prefer an unguessable capability URL, or hold the secret in a proxy. `wodin validate` warns on credential-shaped headers.

section.description: A block of the workout. Holds exercises (movements with sets), rounds (a round > movements hierarchy), or both. Its id keys the block's note and RPE in the result when the block has a footer — see format.

name.description: Shown as the section rule, e.g. "Warm-up".

benchmark.description: Marks a named benchmark (Diane, Murph). Girls and heroes are max effort by definition, so asking for an RPE is noise: the block's RPE pill is not drawn and the result records rpe 11 with rpeAssumed: true under sections[id]. Override with `rpe`.

rpe.description: Whether to ask for this block's RPE. Absent: ask, or assume 11 when `benchmark` is set. An assumed value is recorded as sections[id].rpe with rpeAssumed: true, never in exerciseRpe. "hide" records nothing.

rounds.description: Rounds as a hierarchy: round > movements. Compact on purpose — an entry with `movements` starts a new round; an entry without them reuses the previous round's movements. `reps` on a round replaces the reps of every rep-based movement in it (reps, weight_reps, carry), so 21-15-9 is three short entries. `repeat: n` adds n more copies — of the previous round when the entry has neither movements nor reps, otherwise of the entry itself. The first entry must have movements. When format.rounds is larger than what this expands to, the last round is copied up to it (except amrap, whose rounds are an open-ended template). Round movements are logged in result.sections, never in result.log.

optional.description: Scaling options, drawn as toggle pills at the top of the block. The athlete taps the ones they used; the result records them in `optional` as { id: true }.

modifiers.description: Optional add-ons such as a weight vest. Drawn exactly like `optional` pills but recorded separately: result `modifiers` lists every modifier as true or false, because doing it without the vest is itself an answer.

format.description: How the section is run and scored. Drives the header above the block ("CONDITIONING · FOR TIME · 21-15-9", "Cap 15:00") and, when score is anything but none, a score box after it. A section with rounds, or a score other than none, gets one block footer — score, then RPE and note keyed by the section id — instead of per-exercise pills.

type.description: tabata/intervals: fixed work and rest efforts. emom: one effort at the start of every interval. for_time: finish the work as fast as possible. amrap: as many rounds as possible before the cap. circuit: rounds of movements back to back, unscored by default.

rounds.description: How many rounds or intervals. With a rounds[] list shorter than this, the last round repeats up to the count. A tabata or emom with exercises and no rounds[] derives its rounds: one movement per exercise, from that exercise's first set, repeated this many times — so N rounds are never written by hand. The rounds then replace the exercises' set rows, and the result records them under sections[id].rounds instead of log.

restSec.description: tabata/intervals: rest after each work interval. for_time/circuit: rest after each round.

intervalSec.description: Interval length for emom, seconds — 60 for a classic EMOM.

capSec.description: Time cap, seconds. The AMRAP's duration; the cut-off on a for_time piece.

score.description: What the score box asks for. time: a finish time. rounds_reps: completed rounds plus extra reps (AMRAP). total_reps: one rep count. none or absent: no score box.

round.description: One entry in a section's rounds list. See section.rounds for how entries expand.

reps.description: Reps for every rep-based movement in this round; cardio and time movements are untouched.

roundMovement.description: One movement inside a round. Flat — a round is already one pass, so there is no sets[]. The fields mean what they mean on a set; kind picks the layout, and a round may mix kinds (a run, then swings, then pull-ups).

movement.description: Canonical name, same rules as exercise.movement.

load.description: The load this option implies, in units.load, for a scaled weight.

optional.description: Always true today: a modifier is offered, never imposed.

partition.description: How the athlete may break up the reps. free: any way they like. unbroken: in one go. { max: n }: no more than n per set. Shown as a hint under the movement name.

loadBwMult.description: Load as a multiple of bodyweight — 1.5 means 1.5× BW. Shown as a chip; the load field stays open for the absolute number actually lifted, which the plan cannot know.

exercise.description: One movement and its sets. The athlete's note attaches here — one per exercise, never one per set.

movement.description: The exercise's canonical name and nothing else — "Row", not "Easy row" or "Row 500m". Two reasons. It is searched verbatim to build the form-check link, and adjectives wreck the results. And it is the movement's identity: anything tracking progress across sessions matches on this, so "Easy row" and "Row 500m" would look like two unrelated exercises. Session-specific detail goes in `cue` ("easy pace", "8 per leg", "Outdoors", "Bodyweight") — modifiers like outdoor or bodyweight are never part of the name, while equipment that makes it a different lift (Barbell deadlift, Kettlebell swing) stays in the name. Training intent goes in `tag` ("Pump"), and the prescription in `sets`.

kind.description: Which field layout to draw. Set it explicitly — it cannot be inferred reliably, because a field the athlete is meant to fill is null in the plan too.

tag.description: Short classifier shown before the cue, e.g. "Work set", "Engine", "Hypertrophy".

cue.description: The coach's line — what to focus on. Agent to athlete. Distinct from the athlete's own note, which only exists in the result.

link.description: Where the movement name links to. Omit it and the page builds a YouTube search for "<movement> form", so a form check is always one tap away. Set it to point at a specific demonstration — your own video, a coaching cue you trust, an ExRx page — instead.

intervalSlot.description: For an emom that alternates movements: A runs on odd intervals, B on even ones. Drawn as a chip before the name. Leave it off when every interval is the same movement.

set.description: One prescription row, rendered as "Set 1", "Set 2". Which of these fields are drawn is decided by the exercise's kind. A null field that the athlete is expected to supply should name itself in athleteFills.

kind.description: Overrides the exercise's kind for this row alone. Rarely needed.

loadType.description: Use instead of load:0 for unweighted work. Renders as "BW".

distanceUnit.description: Overrides units.distance for this row — a carry in ft alongside a row in m.

pace.description: Value and denominator together; the denominator becomes the field's unit suffix.

athleteFills.description: Names the field the athlete is expected to supply, for a partial prescription — e.g. distance and pace given, athlete fills duration.

note.description: Not used in a plan. Athlete notes live on the exercise and only exist in a result. Present here only so a round-tripped document does not fail validation.

rpeSetting.description: "ask": draw the RPE pill and record only what is tapped (the default). "hide": no pill, nothing recorded. A number 1–11: no pill; that value is recorded with rpeAssumed: true. 11 sits beyond the 1–10 scale on purpose, so an assumed max effort can never be confused with a tapped value. An assumed value is never prefilled into a control.

kind.description: weight_reps: load × reps. reps: reps only. time: a single duration. cardio: pace + distance + time on one row, any two implying the third. carry: load × reps + distance.

id.description: Optional on input — the renderer assigns ids positionally when absent. Required in a result, where entries are keyed "<exerciseId>.<setId>".
